name: publicWeb_getPageLayout
description: Returns the saved Puck page layout JSON blob for a kennel. Uses LEFT JOIN so kennels without a KennelWebsite row return one row with PageLayoutJson = NULL rather than zero rows (which the shim would misread as 404). Callers fall back to the hardcoded default layout when the value is NULL. No authentication required.

parameters.name: KennelSlug
parameters.description: URL slug of the kennel whose layout to load

rowsets.name: PageLayoutResult
rowsets.description: Always one row for a valid active kennel. Zero rows means kennel not found or inactive — shim returns 404. One row with PageLayoutJson NULL means the kennel exists but has no saved layout yet.

columns.name: PageLayoutJson
columns.description: JSON blob of shape PageLayoutBlob = Partial<Record<PageType, Data>> where PageType is 'home'|'runs'|'about'|'events'|'songs'|'stats'. NULL when no layout has been saved.

codeSmells.detail: Returns the layout even when the kennel website is disabled (Enabled = 0). This is intentional — the admin editor needs to load the layout regardless of published state — but callers rendering the public page should independently check WebsiteEnabled before rendering.

breakingChangeRules: Never change the zero-row = 404 / null-value = no layout contract — Next.js callers depend on this distinction
Never change from LEFT JOIN to INNER JOIN — that would break the null-layout signal
